subcodes.first_line: Omin herlige Herre! Hjelp meg til å avstå fra enhver avvikende tilbøyelighet; til å holde enhver opprørsk lidenskap i tø
subcodes.notes: X = documented-absence from the Phelps inventory of authenticated Abdul-Baha texts (provisional — see caveat). Identity: the prayer O my Glorious Lord Help me to refrain from every irregular inclination to subdue every rebellious passion to purify the motives of my conduct to acquire the meekness which no provocation can ruffle the patience which no affliction can overwhelm the integrity which no self-interest can shake that I may be qualified to serve Thee and to teach Thy Word. ATTRIBUTED to Abdul-Baha but AUTHENTICITY FORMALLY QUESTIONED by the Universal House of Justice (2001): no authentic original located. Published in Some Bahai Prayers no 72 p 77 and downstream prayer books. Same CATEGORY as the famous Western-era questioned prayers Make me a hollow reed and Refresh and gladden my spirit (Joop). CAVEAT (Joop): some questioned-authenticity prayers still carry an OLD or REMOVED Phelps code, OR turn out to be fragments of a recorded TALK with an ABU utterance code — e.g. Refresh and gladden my spirit is embedded in ABU1863. Checked here: 0 corpus hits across ALL languages on both English translation variants, and no inventory first-line match (2026-06-09); but such prayers hide MID-TALK so a removed/utterance code cannot be fully excluded from first-lines alone. FOR PHELPS: if an old/removed code, an ABU talk-fragment, or a later-authenticated original is located, SUPERSEDE this X with it. Norwegian row (bahaiprayers.net source_id 3584) retained as witness text. Minted 2026-06-09 (loop) at Joop request. [2026-06-12 XT migration (Joop): X-codes with uncertain author moved from XAB/XBH to XT (X+TMP semantics — identity absent AND tier unknown; the old prefix asserted an author the scrape could not support; cf. 16-of-16 XAB→BH resolutions on 2026-06-11). Old code preserved here: was XT00129.]
